subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should this Telegram/ACP completed-action confabulation be handled as a narrow core source-channel finalization bug, as a ClawHub claim-verification plugin, or as a split where core only adds missing hooks/semantics?
rationale: Current main has prompt guidance and narrow private-final diagnostics, while the related broad claim-verification request was already closed as plugin scope; choosing the boundary changes privacy, delivery, and plugin API policy.

options.title: Split Core And Plugin Scope
options.body: Keep this issue open for Telegram/ACP source-channel semantics and live repro, and route broad claim-verification policy to ClawHub/plugin work unless an API gap appears.

options.title: Make Core Verify Claims
options.body: Define a built-in finalization policy that warns or blocks unsupported completed-action claims across source-channel turns, accepting the larger compatibility and product footprint.

options.title: Close As Plugin Scope
options.body: Treat the remaining completed-action verification as covered by the ClawHub direction from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/68051 after documenting the handoff.

recommendation.title: Split Core And Plugin Scope
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for Telegram/ACP source-channel semantics and live repro, and route broad claim-verification policy to ClawHub/plugin work unless an API gap appears.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete provided the clearest existing product-policy signal by closing the broad claim-verification request as ClawHub/plugin scope and is connected to adjacent delivery/finalization history.
